full_judgment: 3. On 10-3-2005 the defendant Nos.I-5 and the defendant Nos.6-9 filed two separate applications for rejection of plaintiff under Order 7 rule II read section 11 and section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The defendant's case, in short, is that the father of the defendant Nos.7-9 Anil Ranjan Shyam filed Title Suit No.68 of 1984 praying for declaration that the suit property was not enemy property and the Enemy Case No.58 of 1966-67 was illegal that the said suit was decreed and thereupon, the Government filed Title Appeal No. 60 of 1989 and the appeal was dismissed on contest on 1-4-1996 and thereafter, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (revenue) filed a Civil Revision No. 2836 of 1999 before this Court and on 20-6-1999, the same was summarily rejected on the ground that the application was barred by limitation; that the plaintiff did not take any step against the order of rejection; that Anil Ranjan Shyam then mutated the suit property and a separate Khatian was created in the name of defendant Nos.7-9 and they gifted the said land to the defendant No.6 by the registered deed dated 22-4-2004 and the defendant No.6 got the same mutated in his name, created a separate Khatian and then sold the same to the defendant Nos.1-5 by registered deed and since then the defendant Nos. 1-5 are owning and possessing the suit land; that on 3-8-2004 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet cancelled the mutation created in the name of the defendant No.6 and passed an order to vacate the land within 7 days without serving any notice and without giving any opportunity of being heard and while the defendant No.6 and defendant Nos.1-5 came to know about the matter, they filed two separate Writ Petitions being Writ Petition No.4646 of 2004 and 4443 of 2004 before this Court and obtained Rule and the operation of the memo of cancellation and vacating the suit land was stayed and the Writ Petitions are still pending before this Court; that the plaintiff filed the suit by concealing the facts regarding the Civil Revision and Writ Petition and the suit is barred by res-judicata, barred by limitation and is liable to be rejected.
